cell_type_model: primary mouse osteocyte-like cells; primary calvarial osteoblasts; human A549 and HK-2 epithelial cells
assay_or_perturbation: OSM stimulation with Osmr deletion or receptor blockade; phosphoprotein, gene-expression, and cell-scattering assays
relation_type: OSM activates the gp130-OSMR receptor complex and recruits JAK/STAT and MAPK signaling
pathway_branch: OSM-gp130/OSMR -> JAK1/JAK2-STAT1/STAT3 and Shc1-SHP2-Ras-ERK -> osteoblast/osteocyte remodeling or epithelial-state output
limitations: OSM receptor usage is species- and cell-context dependent; gp130-LIFR can mediate murine OSM responses and OSMR-specific Shc1/ERK effects are not universal. No terminal TF endpoint was assigned for this exact composite.

cell_type_model: primary osteoblasts; transgenic mouse bone and cartilage models; recombinant receptor assays
assay_or_perturbation: Osteocrin expression and conditioned-medium assays; saturable NPR-C binding; Ostn transgenic and CNP/Npr3 genetic interaction studies
relation_type: Direct OSTN-NPR3 binding alters natriuretic-peptide clearance and extracellular ligand availability; NPR3 lacks a canonical catalytic cytosolic signaling domain
pathway_branch: OSTN-NPR3 -> reduced NPR3-mediated CNP clearance -> increased CNP-NPR2 bone-growth signaling
limitations: The evidence supports a clearance-receptor interaction and an indirect effect on CNP/NPR2, not an intracellular NPR3 relay. NPR3-dependent bone output is mediated by altered extracellular natriuretic-peptide availability.

cell_type_model: stable heterologous CHO/HEK receptor-expression systems; human and murine receptor panels
assay_or_perturbation: Oxytocin binding and second-messenger functional profiling across OTR, V1aR, V1bR, and V2R; receptor-selective peptide comparison
relation_type: Oxytocin exhibits context- and species-dependent pharmacological activity at AVPR1A/V1aR
pathway_branch: OXT-AVPR1A/V1aR -> GPCR IP1/Ca2+ or PLC-linked pharmacology in recombinant receptor assays
limitations: Cross-reactivity and potency vary strongly with species, receptor expression system, peptide concentration, and assay readout; no OXT-specific AVPR1A downstream cellular endpoint was resolved.

cell_type_model: stable heterologous CHO receptor-expression systems; rat AVP/OT receptor panels
assay_or_perturbation: Oxytocin/vasopressin analog binding and functional assays across V1b and related receptors
relation_type: Oxytocin has measurable cross-reactive pharmacology at AVPR1B/V1bR but the exact endogenous-ligand relay is not resolved
pathway_branch: OXT-AVPR1B/V1bR -> context-dependent GPCR second-messenger response
limitations: Most selective V1b studies use vasopressin analogs rather than native oxytocin; receptor cross-reactivity does not establish a physiological OXT-AVPR1B pathway or a terminal TF.

cell_type_model: heterologous receptor-expression systems; LLC-PK1 renal epithelial cells
assay_or_perturbation: OT/AVP receptor binding and cAMP/IP1 assays under normal and renal medullary pH/osmolality conditions
relation_type: Oxytocin shows weak or condition-dependent AVPR2/V2R pharmacology without a validated exact-pair cellular relay
pathway_branch: OXT-AVPR2/V2R -> context-dependent cAMP pharmacology
limitations: A renal medullary study found no OXT-V2R binding under acidic hyperosmotic conditions; recombinant cross-panel activity is not evidence for a physiological OXT-AVPR2 relay.

cell_type_model: human myometrial membrane preparations; heterologous CHO receptor-expression systems
assay_or_perturbation: Oxytocin stimulation of solubilized myometrial membranes and reconstituted OTR-Galpha-PLC-delta1 complex; receptor-family second-messenger assays
relation_type: Oxytocin activates OXTR/OTR through Gq-linked PLC and intracellular calcium signaling
pathway_branch: OXT-OXTR -> Gq-PLC-delta1/IP3-Ca2+ -> myometrial contractile and reproductive output
limitations: The direct PLC assay is biochemical and myometrial; receptor coupling and downstream effects vary with tissue and G-protein context. No terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: HepG2/HuH7 hepatocytes; CHO and HEK293 cells; mouse liver and knockout models
assay_or_perturbation: PCSK9 addition or depletion; co-immunoprecipitation, endocytosis, lysosomal trafficking, APLP2 loss-of-function and rescue assays
relation_type: Direct PCSK9-APLP2 interaction promotes PCSK9 internalization and lysosomal routing
pathway_branch: PCSK9-APLP2 -> endocytosis/lysosomal delivery -> PCSK9 and LDLR-family receptor turnover
limitations: APLP2 is a trafficking/sorting partner rather than a canonical signal-transducing receptor; the evidence does not support an intracellular kinase or TF relay through APLP2.

cell_type_model: 3T3-L1 adipocytes; HepG2 cells; primary mouse adipocytes, liver, and visceral adipose tissue
assay_or_perturbation: Recombinant or overexpressed PCSK9; SPR, co-immunoprecipitation, confocal imaging, proteasome/lysosome inhibitors, Pcsk9 knockdown and knockout
relation_type: Direct PCSK9-CD36 binding promotes receptor degradation and changes fatty-acid/oxLDL uptake
pathway_branch: PCSK9-CD36 -> proteasome-associated trafficking and lysosomal degradation -> reduced CD36-dependent lipid uptake
limitations: The measured output is receptor turnover and lipid transport, not receptor-proximal intracellular signaling; the proteasome/lysosome mechanism is not a TF relay.

cell_type_model: Huh7 and CHO/CHO-A7 cells; recombinant PCSK9 and CD81/LDLR expression systems
assay_or_perturbation: PCSK9 gain- and loss-of-function mutants; proximity ligation, co-immunoprecipitation, immunocytochemistry, receptor degradation assays
relation_type: PCSK9 interacts with CD81 and promotes CD81 degradation through intracellular trafficking
pathway_branch: PCSK9-CD81 -> endocytosis/lysosomal degradation, strengthened by LDLR context
limitations: CD81 is a tetraspanin trafficking partner in this context; no CD81-dependent receptor-proximal kinase or transcriptional relay was demonstrated.

cell_type_model: HepG2/HuH7 hepatocytes; HEK293 cells; primary fibroblasts and mouse models
assay_or_perturbation: PCSK9 addition, receptor-domain mutants, lysosome/protease inhibition, live-cell imaging, siRNA and targeted disruption
relation_type: Direct PCSK9-LDLR binding reroutes LDLR from recycling endosomes to lysosomal degradation
pathway_branch: PCSK9-LDLR -> acidic-endosome retention/caveolin- or sorting-dependent trafficking -> lysosomal LDLR loss and reduced LDL uptake
limitations: The molecularly direct outcome is receptor trafficking and degradation, not an intracellular signaling relay.

cell_type_model: recombinant LDLR-family receptor assays; cultured hepatocytes and heterologous cells; mouse brain comparator models
assay_or_perturbation: PCSK9 binding and degradation assays for ApoER2/LRP8; receptor-family competition and APLP2/LDLR perturbations
relation_type: Direct PCSK9-LRP8/ApoER2 binding targets the receptor for endocytic/lysosomal degradation
pathway_branch: PCSK9-LRP8/ApoER2 -> LDLR-family endocytosis and lysosomal turnover -> altered ApoER2 availability
limitations: Evidence is strongest for recombinant receptor and cultured-cell degradation; adult brain studies report tissue-context differences. No LRP8-specific intracellular relay or TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: primary CD4+ T cells; antigen-presenting-cell/T-cell coculture; supported-lipid-bilayer PD-1 microcluster system
assay_or_perturbation: PD-L2 ligation with TCR stimulation; SHP-2 phosphorylation, microcluster imaging, proliferation and cytokine assays
relation_type: PD-L2 binding activates the inhibitory PD-1 ITSM/SHP2 receptor-proximal checkpoint relay
pathway_branch: PD-L2-PD-1 -> PD-1 phosphorylation/SHP2 recruitment -> TCR-proximal dephosphorylation -> reduced T-cell proliferation and cytokines
limitations: PD-1 signaling is co-receptor and antigen-context dependent; the evidence supports inhibitory relay architecture but not a unique terminal TF endpoint for this ligand pair.

cell_type_model: CLEC-2-transfected DT-40 cells; primary platelets/megakaryocytes; podoplanin-expressing renal and melanoma cells
assay_or_perturbation: Podoplanin binding/crosslinking; CLEC-2 YXXL phosphorylation, Src/Syk inhibition, PLCgamma2 readouts, platelet aggregation and Clec1b-deficient mouse metastasis
relation_type: Podoplanin ligates CLEC-2/CLEC1B and activates its hemITAM-Src-Syk platelet relay
pathway_branch: PDPN-CLEC1B -> Src phosphorylation of hemITAM -> Syk-LAT/SLP76-BTK-PLCgamma2 -> Ca2+/PKC and platelet aggregation
limitations: CLEC-2 is a platelet/megakaryocyte receptor and signaling depends on ligand multimerization/crosslinking; tumor-metastasis outputs do not establish a universal endpoint.

cell_type_model: primary neutrophils and monocytes; mouse and human microglia/glial cultures; neuroinflammation models
assay_or_perturbation: PGLYRP1-peptidoglycan complex binding, TREM1 reporter/activation assays, TREM1 inhibition, Pglyrp1 knockdown, and Syk/ERK inhibition
relation_type: PGLYRP1, especially when multimerized or complexed with peptidoglycan, activates TREM1-DAP12/Syk signaling
pathway_branch: PGLYRP1-TREM1 -> DAP12-Syk-ERK1/2 -> STAT3 and inflammatory glial/myeloid outputs
limitations: Soluble monomeric PGLYRP1 may be insufficient; multimerization or microbial-cell-wall context can be required. STAT3 was measured in the microglial study but is retained as a provisional Module22A endpoint.

cell_type_model: diet-induced-obesity mouse tumor models; primary/immortalized retinal pigment epithelial cells; monocytes/macrophages
assay_or_perturbation: PlGF stimulation; Flt1 tyrosine-kinase deletion or blockade; phospho-AKT/ERK/p38 assays, cytokine/chemotaxis and tumor-growth readouts
relation_type: PlGF activates VEGFR1/FLT1-dependent receptor-proximal PI3K-AKT, ERK and p38 branches
pathway_branch: PlGF-FLT1 -> VEGFR1-TK -> PI3K-AKT/ERK/p38 -> macrophage polarization, chemotaxis and tumor/RPE inflammatory output
limitations: FLT1 signaling is weak and highly cell-context dependent; some effects involve VEGFR2 transactivation or noncanonical endothelial/macrophage interactions. No terminal TF endpoint was assigned.

cell_type_model: recombinant sPLA2-X and PLA2R1-expressing cells; mouse airway/colitis models; human lung macrophage and airway epithelial contexts
assay_or_perturbation: PLA2G10/sPLA2-X binding and PLA2R1 internalization/clearance; Pla2g10-deficient and overexpression perturbations
relation_type: PLA2G10 is a high-affinity PLA2R1 ligand and can be internalized/cleared; enzymatic lipid mediator effects are distinct from receptor binding
pathway_branch: sPLA2-X-PLA2R1 -> receptor-mediated uptake/clearance; parallel sPLA2-X lipid hydrolysis -> PUFA/eicosanoid and inflammatory outputs
limitations: The exact receptor-proximal intracellular pathway remains unresolved; many phenotypes are due to extracellular phospholipid hydrolysis rather than PLA2R1 signaling. No terminal TF endpoint was assigned.

cell_type_model: COS-7 and CHO cells expressing uPAR; human endothelial cells; uPAR-mutant and integrin/EGFR perturbation systems
assay_or_perturbation: uPA/ScuPA stimulation; uPAR cleavage-resistant mutants, EGFR/integrin inhibition, FAK/Src/Rac/ERK/Akt assays and migration/angiogenesis models
relation_type: uPA binding to uPAR initiates a receptor-containing multiprotein relay involving integrins, EGFR, Src/FAK/Rac and ERK/PI3K-Akt
pathway_branch: uPA-uPAR -> alpha3/alpha5beta1-integrin and EGFR transactivation -> FAK/Src-Rac-ERK and PI3K-Akt -> migration, adhesion or angiogenesis
limitations: uPAR is GPI-anchored and signals through heterogeneous co-receptor complexes; cleavage state, integrin composition, EGFR abundance, and uPA form alter the branch. No universal terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: M6P/IGF2R-silenced human cell lines; IGF2R-knockout/rescue mouse fibroblasts; primary macrophages and apoptotic-cell efferocytosis models
assay_or_perturbation: Fluorescent plasminogen internalization; IGF2R knockdown/knockout/rescue; receptor-blocking antibody; plasminogen-coated apoptotic-cell uptake and TNF-alpha assays
relation_type: IGF2R/M6P-IGF2R binds and internalizes plasminogen and controls its activation/clearance rather than functioning as a canonical signaling receptor
pathway_branch: PLG-IGF2R -> endocytic uptake and regulation of cell-surface plasmin generation -> efferocytosis and extracellular proteolysis
limitations: IGF2R has multiple sorting functions and the reported outputs depend on uPAR, lipid rafts, macrophage differentiation, or apoptotic-cell context. No direct IGF2R cytosolic relay or TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: monocyte progenitors; primary human and mouse monocytes/macrophages; peritonitis and cell-migration models
assay_or_perturbation: Plasminogen binding, Plg-RKT expression/deletion or antibody blockade, cell-surface plasmin activation and chemotaxis/migration assays
relation_type: Direct plasminogen binding to the C-terminal lysine of PLGRKT promotes cell-surface plasmin generation and proteolytic migration
pathway_branch: PLG-PLGRKT -> cell-surface plasmin activation -> extracellular-matrix degradation -> monocyte/macrophage migration and recruitment
limitations: PLGRKT is a membrane plasminogen receptor, but the evidence resolves extracellular proteolysis and functional migration rather than an intracellular PLGRKT kinase/adaptor relay.

cell_type_model: J774 macrophages; mouse PLTP heterozygous/knockout or overexpression models; ABCA1-upregulated macrophages
assay_or_perturbation: PLTP deficiency/overexpression; cAMP induction of ABCA1; radiolabeled cholesterol efflux and reverse-cholesterol-transport assays
relation_type: PLTP functionally promotes or modulates ABCA1-dependent phospholipid/cholesterol efflux; direct PLTP-ABCA1 binding or intracellular relay was not established
pathway_branch: PLTP-ABCA1 -> extracellular phospholipid transfer/ABCA1-dependent efflux -> HDL formation and macrophage reverse cholesterol transport
limitations: ABCA1 is an ATP-binding cassette transporter rather than a classical ligand-activated receptor; the exact pair is supported at the functional transport layer only and must not be treated as a direct molecular signaling edge.

cell_type_model: CHO cells expressing ORL1/OPRL1; rat olfactory-bulb membrane layers; heterologous receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: Nociceptin stimulation; pertussis-toxin, PLC/PKC, PI3K and Ras/SOS inhibition; MAPK, GTPgammaS and adenylyl-cyclase assays
relation_type: Nociceptin activates OPRL1/NOP through Gi/o and Gbeta-gamma-dependent PLC/PI3K-MAPK branches
pathway_branch: PNOC-nociceptin-OPRL1 -> Gi/o-Gbeta-gamma and PLC/PKC or PI3K-SOS-Ras -> ERK/MAPK and tissue-specific cAMP modulation
limitations: OPRL1 coupling is tissue and assay dependent, with inhibitory or stimulatory adenylyl-cyclase effects in distinct olfactory-bulb layers; no terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: Nb2 pre-T cells; HC11 mammary epithelial cells; rat mammary gland and liver; mammary epithelial coculture
assay_or_perturbation: PRL stimulation or antibody-mediated PRLR dimerization; JAK2/STAT5 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, MAPK/Grb2 cross-talk, tissue-specific lactogenesis assays
relation_type: PRL activates the cytokine-receptor PRLR-JAK2 relay with STAT5 and context-dependent MAPK/PI3K branches
pathway_branch: PRL-PRLR -> receptor-associated JAK2 -> STAT5 and Grb2/Ras-MAPK or PI3K -> mammary differentiation/lactogenesis and proliferation
limitations: PRLR isoform, tissue, and hormonal state determine signaling; liver can express PRLR/JAK2 without the mammary STAT5 response. STAT5 is a measured downstream endpoint, not a direct PRLR-TF interaction.

cell_type_model: rat GH3, AtT20, and RC-4B/C pituitary cell lines; recombinant GPR10/PRLHR-expressing HEK293/CHO cells
assay_or_perturbation: PrRP binding, calcium/inositol-phosphate and cAMP assays; ERK/JNK/CREB phosphorylation; PrRP analog stimulation and receptor expression
relation_type: PrRP activates PRLHR/GPR10 with cell-context-dependent Gi/o and Gq/11-PLC-Ca2+ coupling
pathway_branch: PRLH-PrRP-PRLHR/GPR10 -> Gi/o or Gq/11-PLC-Ca2+/PKC -> ERK/JNK and CREB -> pituitary hormone release or neuroendocrine output
limitations: Coupling differs between recombinant systems and endogenous pituitary cells; PrRP analogs and receptor-family cross-reactivity complicate physiological branch assignment. CREB phosphorylation was measured in endogenous receptor-expressing pituitary cells and is provisional for Module22A.

cell_type_model: primary human endothelial cells/HUVECs; EPCR/PAR1-transfected fibroblasts and HeLa cells; mouse inflammatory models
assay_or_perturbation: Protein C/APC binding or EPCR occupancy; PAR1 cleavage, beta-arrestin recruitment, MAPK/PI3K-Akt/Rac1 assays, gene-silencing and barrier-protection studies
relation_type: Protein C/activated protein C binding to EPCR/PROCR organizes an activation-state-dependent PAR1 cytoprotective relay
pathway_branch: PROC-PROCR/EPCR -> thrombin activation to APC and EPCR occupancy -> PAR1/beta-arrestin or PI3K-Akt-Rac1 -> endothelial barrier and anti-inflammatory output
limitations: Zymogen protein C binding to EPCR is not by itself PAR1 activation; the strongest relay evidence uses activated protein C or EPCR-occupied thrombin. PAR1 is the downstream signaling receptor and no terminal TF endpoint was assigned.

cell_type_model: human PROKR1-Ishikawa endometrial cells; CHO cells expressing PKR1/PROKR1; early-pregnancy and vascular-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: PROK1 stimulation; Gq, PLC, Src, EGFR and MEK inhibition; inositol-phosphate, phospho-ERK/Akt and COX-2 gene-expression assays
relation_type: PROK1 activates PROKR1/PKR1 through Gq-PLC-Ca2+ with Src/EGFR transactivation and ERK/Akt outputs
pathway_branch: PROK1-PROKR1 -> Gq-PLC-Ca2+-c-Src-EGFR-MEK-ERK1/2 and Akt -> COX-2 expression, vascular or endometrial cell function
limitations: The best-resolved mechanism is in engineered or epithelial cell systems and includes EGFR transactivation; PROKR1 and PROKR2 can be co-expressed in tissues, so branch specificity is context dependent. No terminal TF endpoint was assigned.
